next_steps: Redwood to share POC runbook and pricing worksheet
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and 2 week logs
action_items: Maya - Send POC runbook + security pack - 2026-12-01
Laura - Export last 2 weeks traffic profile and sample payloads - 2026-11-30

summary: POC scoping focused on capacity sizing and autoscaling strategy. Customer has variable QPS with spiky peak events; interested in reserved GPUs + burst pool and graceful fallback to smaller models. Success criteria: maintain p95 latency < 350ms for short responses and < 1s for long responses, 99% availability, and cost target of <$0.12 per 1k tokens. Timeline: 4 week POC with benchmark week in week 2.
transcript: 00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off. 00:05 Marco: cool, thanks, we have Ravi, Laura and me on call. 00:10 Maya: perfect, quick intros - I'm Maya AE at Redwood, Ben SE, Nina solutions. 00:20 Ravi: hey, ravi here, head of ml at solstice, we've got a pilot to validate inference economics and latency. 00:30 Ben: great, can you describe current traffic? 00:35 Laura: yeah, so baseline ca 20 qps steady during business hours, but we have spikes up to 450 qps during batch runs and 1k qps for short bursts (few minutes) when promotions run, the payloads are short: 30-120 tokens in/out typically. 00:55 Ben: ok interesting, so distribution is mostly short requests, tail is bursts. what's your p99SLA target? 01:02 Ravi: ideally p95 under 300-350ms for short replies, p95 under 1s for longer 400-800 token outputs. cost target is rough: we want under $0.12 per 1k tokens to be viable. 01:18 Maya: makes sense. for the POC we typically do reserved capacity plus a burst policy. reserved ensures predictable latency for baseline qps, burst pool handles spikes. 01:28 Marco: how many GPUs are we talking? we run a Llama-v2-ish open model, 70B opt and also smaller 13B variants for fallbacks. 01:37 Ben: for 20 qps baseline with short responses you can get away with 1-2 A100-style GPUs depending on batch settings; but we'll size using per-token throughput estimates. during bursts we recommend a 2-3 GPU burst pool, plus auto-failover to a smaller 13B replica. 01:56 Laura: can you explain the failover and fallback policy? i've seen weird behavior elsewhere where fallback increases latency. 02:03 Ben: yep, good point. fallback should be a graceful route: first route to primary model on reserved pool, if queue/backlog grows beyond threshold (e.g., queuing delay > 100ms or CPU/GPU util > 85%) we divert new requests to a cheaper 13B variant with compatible API. existing KV cache for ongoing sessions stays on the primary if possible; otherwise we accept cold-start penalties. 02:25 Ravi: hmm compatibility - we need deterministic-ish outputs for ranking feature. will smaller model break things? 02:31 Maya: that's part of the success criteria — we'll do quality regressions tied to specific prompts. benchmark will include accuracy/regression tests; if quality drop is > 5% on the eval set, fallback won't be allowed for that endpoint. 02:45 Marco: ok that helps. what's the suggested autoscale policy timing? like scale down fast, scale up slow? 02:52 Ben: typical pattern: fast scale up (minutes) with burst pool warmers and pre-warming strategies, slower scale down (cooldown 10-20 minutes) to avoid thrash. We also recommend predictive autoscaling based on schedule (promotions) and rolling reserve for known events. 03:10 Laura: do you do prefix/KV caching across instances? 03:14 Ben: yes, Redwood supports prefix and KV caching; we can keep hot prefixes in memory for low-latency paths and share caches when using same model variant on same pool. cache hit rates will heavily affect effective throughput. 03:27 Ravi: for the POC, our success criteria — list that out for us. 03:32 Maya: ok success criteria: 1) performance: meet p95 latency targets (<=350ms short, <=1s long) under baseline and at 75% of peak burst, 2) reliability: 99% availability during POC, 3) quality: less than 5% regression on our eval prompt set, 4) cost: demonstrate estimated unit cost under your target (<= $0.12/1k tokens) with recommended batching/quantization settings, 5) operational: Redwood provide logs, auditing, and SOC2-ish docs for infra review. 04:05 Marco: timeline? 04:08 Maya: recommended 4 week POC: week 0: kickoff and infra + security onboarding (VPC, keys), week 1: baseline bench and small runs, week 2: full benchmark including reserved + burst tests and quality evals, week 3: tunings and repeat runs, week 4: handover + decision. 04:26 Laura: security — we need SSO, KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency notes. can you provide a security pack? 04:33 Maya: yes we'll share SOC2 summary, SAML/SSO guide, KMS/HSM integration notes, and network diagrams. we'll send the pack after this call. 04:43 Ravi: can we run on our VPC/on-prem? 04:47 Ben: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; for POC we typically run hosted with dedicated tenant or dedicated capacity in customer region. if you need on-prem, lead time is longer and would be treated as a separate engagement. 05:02 Marco: costs for reserved vs hosted? 05:05 Maya: rough numbers in the pricing worksheet we'll send — reserved monthly commit reduced unit cost; POC we can offer short term reserved for the trial. Ben: also mention quantization — int8 inference on smaller models can reduce cost by 2-3x but needs compatibility tests. 05:24 Laura: bench specifics — what do you need from us? 05:28 Ben: we need: 1) traffic profile (qps distribution, payload sizes), 2) sample payloads for quality/regression tests, 3) golden eval set of 200-500 prompts, 4) preferred model variants (70B and 13B). 05:44 Laura: ok i'll export logs and payloads, target by end of week. 05:48 Maya: great. for capacity sizing we'll propose: reserved 2 x A100-equivalent for baseline (handles 20-40 qps steady with batching), burst pool of 3 x A100 equiv for spikes up to 400-1k qps with auto-shed to 13B fallback. we'll also supply benchmarks that show p95 under those configs. 06:12 Marco: what about limits and throttling? 06:16 Ben: implement per-route rate limits, token quotas, and prioritized queues for critical routes. also circuit breakers if backend error rate exceeds threshold. 06:26 Ravi: bench success measure for costs — show cost per 1k tokens with current batch settings and alternate quantization profiles. 06:33 Ben: yes we'll run matrix: (reserved-only), (reserved+burst), (reserved+burst+13B fallback), with and without quantization. 06:44 Maya: next steps recap: Maya sends runbook and security pack; Laura sends logs/payloads; Ben prepares bench scripts; schedule 30-minute benchmark run next Wednesday — is that ok for everyone? 06:56 Laura: yes, that's fine. 07:00 Marco: one more question — how do you ensure routing during AZ outages? 07:05 Ben: multi-AZ placement for reserved pools recommended; smart routing will divert to another region/pool automatically but may induce cold starts; we document RTO and predicted latency increase in those cases. 07:18 Ravi: ok, thanks everyone. 07:20 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with email and attach the docs. meeting end.
